title: "Fig. 3 and Fig. S2 - Morning and evening activity peaks"

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Morning (M) and evening (E) activity peaks under constant
# darkness (DD): Culex pipiens and Culex quinquefasciatus entrained
# to short-day (SD, 9L:15D) or long-day (LD, 15L:9D) photoperiods
#
# Overview
#   For each individual, this script detects the M-peak (near the
#   entrainment lights-on time) and the E-peak (near the entrainment
#   lights-off time) in its average DD activity profile, and then
#   compares groups in a 2 x 2 design (species x entrainment
#   photoperiod) on:
#     - the E-to-M peak interval,
#     - the deviation of that interval from the entrained dark-phase
#       length (15 h for SD, 9 h for LD),
#     - the E-peak phase relative to entrainment lights-off, and
#     - the proportion of individuals with a detected M- or E-peak.
#
# Peak detection (adapted from Vaze et al. 2023, J Comp Physiol A)
#   1. Average each individual's activity at each minute of the day
#      over the last DD_DAYS days of the recording.
#   2. Double-plot the 24 h profile (concatenate it with itself to
#      give a 48 h trace) so that peaks near midnight are not
#      truncated.
#   3. Smooth the doubled trace by local regression (loess, span =
#      loess_span).
#   4. Apply a centered moving average (ma_k points) to the loess
#      curve.
#   5. Find the points where the unsmoothed activity crosses the
#      moving-average curve from above to below; these crossings are
#      candidate peaks. Only crossings in the second copy of the
#      double plot (hours 24-48) are kept and converted back to time
#      of day (0-24 h).
#   6. Assign the M-peak and E-peak as the candidate inside a window
#      of +/- half_window_h hours around the entrainment lights-on
#      and lights-off times, respectively. If several candidates fall
#      in a window, the one with the higher value on the
#      moving-average curve is kept.
#
#   Window definition: Vaze et al. classify peaks by the first or
#   second half of the light phase. Here a fixed window of equal
#   width around lights-on and lights-off is used instead, because
#   (a) the assay is in DD, so there is no light phase to divide, and
#   (b) half-photophase windows would be 4.5 h wide for SD but 7.5 h
#   wide for LD, giving the two photoperiods unequal search widths.
#
# Manual verification
#   Individuals lacking a detected M- or E-peak, and individuals whose
#   E-to-M interval is shorter than EM_min_interval_h, are listed for
#   visual review of their activity traces. Reviewed channels are
#   entered in the rescue/exclude lists (see MANUAL VERIFICATION
#   section): a rescued peak is re-extracted with the same method
#   (or, if no crossing exists in the window, taken as the maximum of
#   the loess curve in the window); an excluded peak is set to "not
#   detected". All statistics, exports and plots use the corrected
#   table.
#
# Statistical analysis
#   For each continuous variable, a linear model (species x
#   photoperiod) is fitted and its residuals tested with the
#   Shapiro-Wilk test (alpha = 0.05):
#     - normal residuals: two-way ANOVA (Type II) on the raw scale;
#     - non-normal, strictly positive variable, and normal residuals
#       after log transformation: two-way ANOVA on the log scale;
#     - otherwise: Aligned Rank Transform (ART) ANOVA with ART-C
#       contrasts (ARTool package).
#   Pairwise comparisons among the four groups are Holm-adjusted
#   across all six comparisons; the two species comparisons within
#   each photoperiod are then extracted for reporting and plotting.
#
#   M-peak phase is not analyzed as a separate outcome because
#   M-peak detection was markedly lower in Cx. pipiens SD (58.6%)
#   than in the other three groups (83.3-100%); a phase comparison
#   would rest on a reduced, non-random subset of that group. E-peak
#   detection showed no comparable group-specific loss.
#
#   Peak detection rates are compared with Fisher's exact tests
#   (overall across the four groups, then all six pairs with Holm
#   adjustment). Odds ratios are the odds of detection in group1
#   relative to group2.
#
# Input
#   Four TriKinetics monitor files (1-min bins, one header row), set
#   in INPUT FILES. Columns 11-42 hold activity channels 1-32. The
#   last DD_DAYS days of each recording are analyzed as DD.
#
# Output (written to the working directory)
#   all_indiv_manually_corrected.csv        per-individual peak times
#                                            and derived variables
#   peak_detection_rate_summary.csv          detection counts and %
#   peak_detection_rate_wilson_CI.csv        detection % with 95% CI
#   peak_detection_fisher_test.csv           overall Fisher's tests
#   peak_detection_pairwise_full6_global.csv pairwise Fisher's tests
#   peak_detection_within_photoperiod_extracted.csv
#   threshold_logging_summary.csv            peaks at the window edge
#   EM_interval_group_estimates.csv          interval means and 95% CI
#   shapiro_wilk_results_all_variables.csv
#   omnibus_test_results_all_variables.csv
#   phase_interval_pairwise_full6_global.csv
#   phase_interval_within_photoperiod_extracted.csv
#   phase_interval_statistics_adaptive.csv
#   Fig_EM_interval_*.png, Fig_EM_interval_deviation_*.png,
#   Fig_E_phase_*.png, Fig_peak_detection_rate_SDvsLD.png
#
# Requirements
#   R with tidyverse, zoo, car, ARTool, emmeans and ragg. Species
#   names are italicized with plotmath, and figures are saved with
#   the ragg device so that italic fonts render reliably.
#
# References
#   Vaze KM et al. (2023). J Comp Physiol A (peak detection method).
#   Wobbrock JO, Findlater L, Gergle D, Higgins JJ (2011). The
#     aligned rank transform for nonparametric factorial analyses
#     using only ANOVA procedures. Proc. ACM CHI 2011, 143-146.
#   Elkin LA, Kay M, Higgins JJ, Wobbrock JO (2021). An aligned
#     rank transform procedure for multifactor contrast tests.
#     Proc. ACM UIST 2021, 754-768.
# ============================================================

# Install ARTool and ragg if they are missing.
for (pkg in c("ARTool", "ragg")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(pkg)
}
library(tidyverse)
library(zoo)
library(car)      # for Anova(type = "II"), parametric path only
library(ARTool)   # for art() / anova.art() / art.con()
library(emmeans)  # for model-based contrasts on the parametric path
library(ragg)     # reliable italic font rendering in saved PNGs

# ============================================================
# INPUT FILES (1-min raw)
# ============================================================
pip_SD_file  <- "pipiens_SD.txt"
quin_SD_file <- "quinque_SD.txt"

pip_LD_file  <- "pipiens_LD.txt"
quin_LD_file <- "quinque_LD.txt"

# ============================================================
# ENTRAINMENT LIGHTS-ON / LIGHTS-OFF TIMES (decimal hours)
# Used in DD as the reference times for the M- and E-peak windows.
# ============================================================
SD_LON  <- 8           # 9L:15D entrainment (lights on 8:00)
SD_LOFF <- 17          # lights off 17:00
LD_LON  <- 6 + 3/60    # 15L:9D entrainment (lights on 6:03am)
LD_LOFF <- 21 + 3/60   # lights off 9:03pm

# ============================================================
# ACTIVITY COLUMN LAYOUT
# File columns 11-42 hold activity channels 1-32 (one individual
# per channel).
# ============================================================
activity_start_col <- 11
activity_end_col   <- 42

# Channels (1-32) excluded from each group before analysis.
pip_SD_exclude_ch  <- c(1,3,7)
quin_SD_exclude_ch <- c()
pip_LD_exclude_ch  <- c(8,15,16,26)
quin_LD_exclude_ch <- c(2,6,10,17,19)

# ============================================================
# DD SETTINGS
# ============================================================
DD_DAYS <- 3  # number of days at the end of each recording analyzed as DD

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION SETTINGS
# half_window_h: half-width (h) of the M- and E-peak search windows
#   around lights-on and lights-off; the same for SD and LD.
# loess_span / ma_k: loess smoothing span and moving-average window
#   length (points) of the peak detection method.
# ============================================================
half_window_h <- 3
loess_span    <- 0.02
ma_k          <- 11   # moving-average window over the loess curve; MUST be odd
if (ma_k %% 2 == 0) stop("ma_k must be odd for a symmetric centered moving average.")

# Minimum plausible E-to-M interval (h); shorter intervals are set
# to NA and listed for review.
EM_min_interval_h <- 6

# Dark-phase length during entrainment (h), used as the expected
# E-to-M interval.
expected_interval_h <- c(SD = 15, LD = 9)

# ============================================================
# HELPERS
# ============================================================
# Wrap times to 0-24 h, or to -12 to +12 h (for phase differences).
wrap24 <- function(x) x %% 24
wrap12 <- function(x) ((x + 12) %% 24) - 12
# Convert a channel number to its file column.
ch_to_abscol <- function(ch) activity_start_col + ch - 1

# TRUE for times of day within +/- halfwidth of center, wrapping
# across midnight.
in_centered_window <- function(tod, center, halfwidth) {
  start <- center - halfwidth
  end   <- center + halfwidth
  if (start < 0 || end >= 24) {
    start <- wrap24(start); end <- wrap24(end)
    (tod >= start) | (tod <= end)
  } else {
    (tod >= start) & (tod <= end)
  }
}

# Convert a p-value to a significance label.
sig_stars <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)    ~ "NA",
    p <= 0.0001 ~ "****",
    p <= 0.001  ~ "***",
    p <= 0.01   ~ "**",
    p <= 0.05   ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ "ns"
  )
}

# Line segments for vertical significance brackets (one per panel)
# on the horizontal box plots.
make_bracket_segments <- function(bracket_df, x_col = "x_pos", tick = NULL) {
  if (is.null(tick)) tick <- 0.03 * max(abs(bracket_df[[x_col]]), na.rm = TRUE)
  bind_rows(
    bracket_df %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = .data[[x_col]], xend = .data[[x_col]], y = 1, yend = 2),
    bracket_df %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = .data[[x_col]] - tick, xend = .data[[x_col]], y = 1, yend = 1),
    bracket_df %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = .data[[x_col]] - tick, xend = .data[[x_col]], y = 2, yend = 2)
  )
}

# From the six pairwise comparisons, keep the two species
# comparisons within the same photoperiod.
extract_within_photoperiod <- function(full6_df, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(c("LD", "SD"), function(pp) {
    g1 <- paste0("Cxquin_", pp); g2 <- paste0("Cxpip_", pp)
    m <- full6_df %>% filter((group1 == g1 & group2 == g2) | (group1 == g2 & group2 == g1))
    m %>% mutate(photoperiod = pp) %>% relocate(photoperiod, .after = comparison)
  })
}

# Split an ARTool contrast label ("a,b - c,d") into species and
# photoperiod for each side.
parse_artool_contrast <- function(contrast_str) {
  sides <- str_split(contrast_str, " - ", simplify = TRUE)
  s1 <- str_split(trimws(sides[1]), ",", simplify = TRUE)
  s2 <- str_split(trimws(sides[2]), ",", simplify = TRUE)
  tibble(species1 = trimws(s1[1]), photoperiod1 = trimws(s1[2]),
         species2 = trimws(s2[1]), photoperiod2 = trimws(s2[2]))
}

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION FUNCTIONS (see header for the method)
# ============================================================
# ---- Double-plot a 24 h profile (concatenate it with itself to give
#      a 48 h trace). ----
double_plot_profile <- function(tod, activity) {
  ord <- order(tod)
  tod <- tod[ord]; activity <- activity[ord]
  tibble(
    t        = c(tod, tod + 24),
    activity = c(activity, activity)
  )
}

# ---- Fit a loess curve to the doubled trace, evaluated at the same
#      time points as the data. Returns t, the unsmoothed (doubled)
#      activity and the loess value at each t. ----
get_va_loess_curve <- function(tod, activity, span = loess_span) {
  dp <- double_plot_profile(tod, activity)
  fit <- loess(activity ~ t, data = dp, span = span, degree = 2)
  loess_y <- as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(t = dp$t)))
  tibble(t = dp$t, activity_raw = dp$activity, loess_y = loess_y)
}

# ---- Add the moving average of the loess curve (ma_y) on the same
#      time points. The ends are padded with the first/last loess
#      value so the output has the same length as the input. ----
get_va_curves <- function(tod, activity, span = loess_span, k = ma_k) {
  curve <- get_va_loess_curve(tod, activity, span)
  pad <- (k - 1) / 2
  loess_padded <- c(rep(curve$loess_y[1], pad), curve$loess_y,
                    rep(curve$loess_y[length(curve$loess_y)], pad))
  curve$ma_y <- as.numeric(zoo::rollmean(loess_padded, k = k, align = "center"))
  curve
}

# ---- Find all candidate peaks: points where the unsmoothed activity
#      crosses the moving-average curve from above to below. The
#      crossing time is linearly interpolated between samples. Returns
#      the time of day (from the 24-48 h copy) and the moving-average
#      value at each crossing (y_cross, used only to choose between
#      candidates in a window). ----
find_va_peaks <- function(tod, activity, span = loess_span, k = ma_k) {
  curve <- get_va_curves(tod, activity, span, k)
  diff_y    <- curve$activity_raw - curve$ma_y
  sign_diff <- sign(diff_y)
  cross_idx <- which(diff(sign_diff) != 0)
  if (length(cross_idx) == 0) {
    return(tibble(tod = numeric(0), y_cross = numeric(0)))
  }
  crossings <- purrr::map_dfr(cross_idx, function(i) {
    t1 <- curve$t[i];   t2 <- curve$t[i + 1]
    d1 <- diff_y[i];    d2 <- diff_y[i + 1]
    if (d1 == d2) return(NULL)  # guard against degenerate flat segments
    frac    <- d1 / (d1 - d2)
    t_cross <- t1 + frac * (t2 - t1)
    y_cross <- curve$ma_y[i] + frac * (curve$ma_y[i + 1] - curve$ma_y[i])
    tibble(
      t_cross   = t_cross,
      y_cross   = y_cross,
      direction = if (d1 > 0 && d2 < 0) "peak" else if (d1 < 0 && d2 > 0) "trough" else "flat"
    )
  })
  crossings %>%
    filter(direction == "peak", t_cross >= 24, t_cross < 48) %>%
    transmute(tod = t_cross - 24, y_cross)
}

# ---- Select the candidate peak inside the window (+/- halfwidth)
#      around a reference time; if several qualify, keep the one with
#      the highest y_cross. Returns NA if none. ----
select_va_peak_in_window <- function(peaks_df, center_time, halfwidth) {
  cand <- peaks_df %>% filter(in_centered_window(tod, center_time, halfwidth))
  if (nrow(cand) == 0) {
    return(tibble(tod = NA_real_, y_cross = NA_real_))
  }
  cand %>% arrange(desc(y_cross)) %>% slice(1)
}

# ---- Peak time for a manually rescued peak (confirmed by visual
#      review): uses the same crossing method, or, if there is no
#      crossing in the window, the time of the loess maximum within
#      the window. ----
peak_tod_max_only_va <- function(tod, activity, center_time, halfwidth,
                                 span = loess_span, k = ma_k) {
  va_peaks <- find_va_peaks(tod, activity, span, k)
  sel <- select_va_peak_in_window(va_peaks, center_time, halfwidth)
  if (!is.na(sel$tod)) return(tibble(tod = sel$tod))
  curve <- get_va_loess_curve(tod, activity, span)
  clean <- curve %>% filter(t >= 24, t < 48) %>% mutate(tod = t - 24)
  sub   <- clean %>% filter(in_centered_window(tod, center_time, halfwidth))
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(tibble(tod = NA_real_))
  sub %>% filter(loess_y == max(loess_y)) %>% slice(1) %>%
    transmute(tod)
}

# ============================================================
# 2 x 2 STATISTICAL ANALYSIS (species x photoperiod)
# Selects raw-scale ANOVA, log-scale ANOVA or ART from Shapiro-Wilk
# tests on model residuals (see header). Returns the omnibus table,
# all six Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons, the within-photoperiod
# species comparisons and the values used for plot brackets.
# ============================================================
analyze_2x2_adaptive <- function(df, value_col, label, alpha = 0.05) {
  # Use only finite values (removes NA, NaN and Inf).
  d <- df %>% filter(is.finite(.data[[value_col]]))
  form <- as.formula(paste(value_col, "~ species * photoperiod"))
  mod_raw <- lm(form, data = d)
  sw_raw <- shapiro.test(residuals(mod_raw))

  cat("\n====================================\n")
  cat("Analyzing:", label, "\n")
  cat("====================================\n")
  cat("Shapiro-Wilk on RAW model residuals: W =", round(sw_raw$statistic, 4),
      ", p =", round(sw_raw$p.value, 4), "\n")

  shapiro_log <- list(attempted = FALSE)
  can_log <- all(d[[value_col]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)

  descriptives <- d %>%
    group_by(species, photoperiod) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
              sd = sd(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE), sem = sd / sqrt(n),
              median = median(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  cat("\nDescriptive statistics:\n"); print(descriptives)

  run_parametric <- function(data_used, col_used, scale_used) {
    mod <- lm(as.formula(paste(col_used, "~ species * photoperiod")), data = data_used)
    aov_tab <- car::Anova(mod, type = "II")
    cat("\nTwo-way ANOVA (Type II SS, scale =", scale_used, "):\n"); print(aov_tab)

    em <- emmeans::emmeans(mod, ~ species * photoperiod)
    con <- emmeans::contrast(em, "pairwise", adjust = "holm")
    con_summary <- as_tibble(summary(con))
    cat("\nFull 6-way emmeans contrasts (Holm-corrected across all 6):\n"); print(con_summary)

    posthoc_df <- con_summary %>%
      separate(contrast, into = c("g1", "g2"), sep = " - ") %>%
      transmute(comparison = label,
                group1 = str_replace(trimws(g1), " ", "_"),
                group2 = str_replace(trimws(g2), " ", "_"),
                estimate, SE, df, t_value = t.ratio,
                p_value = p.value, significance = sig_stars(p.value))

    within <- extract_within_photoperiod(posthoc_df, label)
    cat("\nWithin-photoperiod contrasts extracted from the globally-corrected 6-way family",
        "-- this is what's plotted and reported):\n"); print(within)

    bracket_df <- within %>% transmute(photoperiod, p_value)
    subtitle_txt <- sprintf(
      "ANOVA (%s scale, residuals normal) — species p=%.3g, photoperiod p=%.3g, interaction p=%.3g",
      scale_used, aov_tab["species", "Pr(>F)"], aov_tab["photoperiod", "Pr(>F)"],
      aov_tab["species:photoperiod", "Pr(>F)"])

    list(path = "parametric", scale_used = scale_used, descriptives = descriptives,
         omnibus_table = aov_tab, posthoc_df = posthoc_df, within_photoperiod_df = within,
         bracket_df = bracket_df, subtitle = subtitle_txt)
  }

  run_art <- function() {
    m <- art(form, data = d)
    cat("\nARTool alignment diagnostic (summary.art; all values should be ~0):\n")
    print(summary(m))
    aov_tab <- anova(m)
    cat("\nARTool omnibus ANOVA (Type III, the package default for ART):\n"); print(aov_tab)

    con_raw <- art.con(m, "species:photoperiod", adjust = "none")
    con_df <- as_tibble(summary(con_raw))
    parsed <- purrr::map_dfr(con_df$contrast, parse_artool_contrast)
    con_df <- bind_cols(con_df, parsed) %>%
      mutate(p_holm6 = p.adjust(p.value, method = "holm"))

    full6_export <- con_df %>%
      transmute(comparison = label,
                group1 = paste0(species1, "_", photoperiod1),
                group2 = paste0(species2, "_", photoperiod2),
                estimate, SE, df, t_value = t.ratio,
                p_value = p_holm6, significance = sig_stars(p_holm6))
    cat("\nFull 6-way ART-C contrasts via ARTool (Holm-corrected across all 6):\n")
    print(full6_export)

    within <- con_df %>% filter(photoperiod1 == photoperiod2) %>%
      transmute(comparison = label, photoperiod = photoperiod1,
                method = "ART-C (ARTool, dedicated per-contrast alignment)",
                estimate, statistic = t.ratio, df, p_value = p_holm6,
                significance = sig_stars(p_holm6))
    cat("\nWithin-photoperiod contrasts extracted from the globally-corrected 6-way family",
        "-- this is what's plotted and reported):\n"); print(within)

    bracket_df <- within %>% transmute(photoperiod, p_value)
    p_species <- aov_tab$`Pr(>F)`[aov_tab$Term == "species"]
    p_photo   <- aov_tab$`Pr(>F)`[aov_tab$Term == "photoperiod"]
    p_int     <- aov_tab$`Pr(>F)`[aov_tab$Term == "species:photoperiod"]
    subtitle_txt <- sprintf(
      "ART (ARTool, Type III, residuals non-normal) — species p=%.3g, photoperiod p=%.3g, interaction p=%.3g",
      p_species, p_photo, p_int)

    list(path = "nonparametric", scale_used = "raw (rank-based, ARTool)", descriptives = descriptives,
         omnibus_table = aov_tab, art_c_df = full6_export, within_photoperiod_df = within,
         bracket_df = bracket_df, subtitle = subtitle_txt)
  }

  if (sw_raw$p.value >= alpha) {
    cat(" --> RAW NORMAL -> using ANOVA on raw scale.\n")
    result <- run_parametric(d, value_col, "raw")
  } else if (can_log) {
    log_col <- paste0(value_col, "_log")
    d[[log_col]] <- log(d[[value_col]])
    mod_log <- lm(as.formula(paste(log_col, "~ species * photoperiod")), data = d)
    sw_log <- shapiro.test(residuals(mod_log))
    shapiro_log <- list(attempted = TRUE, W = unname(sw_log$statistic), p = sw_log$p.value)
    cat("Shapiro-Wilk on LOG-transformed model residuals: W =", round(sw_log$statistic, 4),
        ", p =", round(sw_log$p.value, 4), "\n")

    if (sw_log$p.value >= alpha) {
      cat(" --> RAW non-normal, LOG NORMAL -> using ANOVA on log scale.\n")
      result <- run_parametric(d, log_col, "log")
    } else {
      cat(" --> RAW non-normal, LOG also non-normal -> using ART (ARTool).\n")
      result <- run_art()
    }
  } else {
    cat(" --> RAW non-normal; variable can be zero/negative so log-transform was NOT attempted -> using ART (ARTool).\n")
    result <- run_art()
  }

  bracket_df <- result$bracket_df %>%
    mutate(label = sig_stars(p_value), photoperiod = factor(photoperiod, levels = c("LD", "SD")))
  result$bracket_df <- bracket_df
  result$label <- label
  result$value_col <- value_col
  result$can_log <- can_log
  result$shapiro_raw_W <- unname(sw_raw$statistic)
  result$shapiro_raw_p <- sw_raw$p.value
  result$shapiro_log <- shapiro_log

  result
}

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION FOR ONE GROUP
# Reads a monitor file, averages each individual's activity over the
# DD window, detects the M- and E-peaks, and returns one row per
# individual with peak times, the E-to-M interval, phases relative to
# lights-on/off, and detection flags. Individuals lacking a peak or
# with an implausibly short interval are printed for manual review.
# ============================================================
extract_phase_offsets <- function(file_path, species, exclude_ch,
                                  LON, LOFF, photoperiod) {
  raw <- readr::read_tsv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  exclude_abs <- ch_to_abscol(exclude_ch)
  keep_abs    <- setdiff(activity_start_col:activity_end_col, exclude_abs)

  if (max(keep_abs) > ncol(raw)) {
    stop(species, " (", photoperiod, "): file has ", ncol(raw),
         " columns but you requested up to col ", max(keep_abs),
         ". Fix activity_start_col/activity_end_col.")
  }

  act <- raw %>%
    select(all_of(names(raw)[keep_abs])) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))

  n_min      <- nrow(act)
  total_days <- ceiling(n_min / 1440)
  dd_start   <- total_days - DD_DAYS + 1
  dd_end     <- total_days

  message(species, " (", photoperiod, "): inferred total_days=", total_days,
          " | using DD days ", dd_start, "-", dd_end, " (last ", DD_DAYS, " days).")

  long_full <- act %>%
    mutate(t_min = row_number() - 1,
           day   = floor(t_min / 1440) + 1,
           tod   = (t_min %% 1440) / 60) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(t_min, day, tod), names_to = "colname", values_to = "activity") %>%
    mutate(
      abscol  = match(colname, names(raw)),
      channel = abscol - activity_start_col + 1
    )

  dd_raw <- long_full %>% filter(day >= dd_start, day <= dd_end)

  avg_raw_profile <- dd_raw %>%
    group_by(channel, tod) %>%
    summarise(activity_mean = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(channel, tod)

  per_indiv <- avg_raw_profile %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    group_modify(~{
      va_peaks <- find_va_peaks(.x$tod, .x$activity_mean)
      M_sel <- select_va_peak_in_window(va_peaks, LON,  half_window_h)
      E_sel <- select_va_peak_in_window(va_peaks, LOFF, half_window_h)

      tibble(
        M_peak_mean_tod  = M_sel$tod,
        E_peak_mean_tod  = E_sel$tod
      )
    }) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      EM_interval_raw  = (M_peak_mean_tod - E_peak_mean_tod) %% 24,
      EM_interval_mean = ifelse(is.na(EM_interval_raw) | EM_interval_raw < EM_min_interval_h,
                                NA_real_, EM_interval_raw),
      species     = species,
      photoperiod = photoperiod,
      M_phase_h   = wrap12(M_peak_mean_tod - LON),
      E_phase_h   = wrap12(E_peak_mean_tod - LOFF),
      has_M_peak  = !is.na(M_peak_mean_tod),
      has_E_peak  = !is.na(E_peak_mean_tod)
    )

  needs_review <- per_indiv %>%
    filter(!has_M_peak | !has_E_peak)

  if (nrow(needs_review) > 0) {
    cat("\n[", species, " ", photoperiod, "] NEEDS MANUAL REVIEW -- no intersection-",
        "defined peak found by the double-plot/loess/moving-average-vs-original method within the ",
        "+/-", half_window_h, "h window. This (has_M_peak/has_E_peak == FALSE), not the ",
        "EM-interval floor below, is the PRIMARY trigger for populating the rescue/",
        "exclude lists in the manual verification layer:\n", sep = "")
    print(needs_review %>% select(channel, has_M_peak, has_E_peak, M_peak_mean_tod, E_peak_mean_tod))
  } else {
    cat("\n[", species, " ", photoperiod, "] All individuals have both peaks detected.\n", sep = "")
  }

  short_interval_flag <- per_indiv %>%
    filter(!is.na(EM_interval_raw) & EM_interval_raw < EM_min_interval_h)

  if (nrow(short_interval_flag) > 0) {
    cat("\n[", species, " ", photoperiod, "] SECONDARY CHECK -- both M and E peaks WERE ",
        "detected, but the resulting interval is implausibly short (<", EM_min_interval_h,
        "h), suggesting a possible mislabeled/spurious peak even though the algorithm ",
        "reported success. Worth a visual check, but this is a secondary flag, not the ",
        "primary review trigger:\n", sep = "")
    print(short_interval_flag %>% select(channel, M_peak_mean_tod, E_peak_mean_tod, EM_interval_raw))
  }

  message(species, " (", photoperiod, "): individuals kept = ", nrow(per_indiv),
          " | channels kept = ", paste(sort(per_indiv$channel), collapse = ", "))

  cat("\n[", species, " ", photoperiod, "] Peak detection outcome per individual",
      " (based on the single averaged 24h profile, not per-day):\n", sep = "")
  print(per_indiv %>% select(channel, has_M_peak, has_E_peak))

  per_indiv
}

# ---- Average DD activity profile (unsmoothed) for one channel, used
#      to re-extract a rescued peak. ----
build_single_channel_profile <- function(file_path, exclude_ch, channel_of_interest) {
  raw <- readr::read_tsv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  exclude_abs <- ch_to_abscol(exclude_ch)
  keep_abs    <- setdiff(activity_start_col:activity_end_col, exclude_abs)

  act <- raw %>%
    select(all_of(names(raw)[keep_abs])) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))

  n_min      <- nrow(act)
  total_days <- ceiling(n_min / 1440)
  dd_start   <- total_days - DD_DAYS + 1
  dd_end     <- total_days

  long_full <- act %>%
    mutate(t_min = row_number() - 1, day = floor(t_min / 1440) + 1, tod = (t_min %% 1440) / 60) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(t_min, day, tod), names_to = "colname", values_to = "activity") %>%
    mutate(abscol = match(colname, names(raw)), channel = abscol - activity_start_col + 1) %>%
    filter(channel == channel_of_interest)

  dd_raw <- long_full %>% filter(day >= dd_start, day <= dd_end)

  dd_raw %>%
    group_by(tod) %>%
    summarise(activity_mean = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(tod)
}

get_rescued_peak <- function(sp, pp, ch, center_time, halfwidth) {
  cfg <- group_config %>% filter(species == sp, photoperiod == pp)
  profile <- build_single_channel_profile(cfg$file[[1]], cfg$exclude_ch[[1]], ch)
  peak_tod_max_only_va(profile$tod, profile$activity_mean, center_time, halfwidth)
}

# ---- Apply the manual calls and recompute the E-to-M interval and
#      its deviation from the expected interval. ----
apply_manual_calls <- function(all_indiv, manual_calls, group_config) {
  result <- all_indiv

  if (nrow(manual_calls) == 0) {
    cat("No manual calls -- returning all_indiv unchanged.\n")
    return(result)
  }

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(manual_calls))) {
    ov <- manual_calls[i, ]

    row_idx <- which(result$species == ov$species & result$photoperiod == ov$photoperiod &
                       result$channel == ov$channel)

    if (length(row_idx) == 0) {
      warning("Manual call did not match any individual and was skipped: species=",
              ov$species, ", photoperiod=", ov$photoperiod, ", channel=", ov$channel,
              ", peak_type=", ov$peak_type, ", call=", ov$manual_call,
              ". Check for a typo in the variable name, a channel already present in ",
              "the exclude_ch list (removed before extraction, so it can never match here), ",
              "or a species/photoperiod spelling mismatch.")
      next
    }

    cfg <- group_config %>% filter(species == ov$species, photoperiod == ov$photoperiod)
    center <- if (ov$peak_type == "M") cfg$LON else cfg$LOFF

    if (ov$manual_call == "real_peak") {
      rescued <- get_rescued_peak(ov$species, ov$photoperiod, ov$channel, center, half_window_h)
      new_tod <- rescued$tod

      if (ov$peak_type == "M") {
        result$M_peak_mean_tod[row_idx] <- new_tod
        result$has_M_peak[row_idx] <- !is.na(new_tod)
        result$M_phase_h[row_idx] <- wrap12(new_tod - cfg$LON)
      } else {
        result$E_peak_mean_tod[row_idx] <- new_tod
        result$has_E_peak[row_idx] <- !is.na(new_tod)
        result$E_phase_h[row_idx] <- wrap12(new_tod - cfg$LOFF)
      }
    } else if (ov$manual_call == "flat") {
      if (ov$peak_type == "M") {
        result$M_peak_mean_tod[row_idx] <- NA_real_
        result$has_M_peak[row_idx] <- FALSE
        result$M_phase_h[row_idx] <- NA_real_
      } else {
        result$E_peak_mean_tod[row_idx] <- NA_real_
        result$has_E_peak[row_idx] <- FALSE
        result$E_phase_h[row_idx] <- NA_real_
      }
    }
  }

  result <- result %>%
    mutate(
      EM_interval_raw = (M_peak_mean_tod - E_peak_mean_tod) %% 24,
      EM_interval_mean = ifelse(is.na(EM_interval_raw) | EM_interval_raw < EM_min_interval_h,
                                NA_real_, EM_interval_raw),
      expected_interval_h = expected_interval_h[as.character(photoperiod)],
      interval_deviation = EM_interval_mean - expected_interval_h
    )

  result
}

# deviation from the expected interval, per species x photoperiod.
# ============================================================
interval_group_summary <- bind_rows(
  all_indiv %>%
    filter(!is.na(EM_interval_mean)) %>%
    group_by(species, photoperiod) %>%
    summarise(
      variable = "EM_interval_mean (hours)",
      n        = n(),
      mean     = mean(EM_interval_mean),
      sd       = sd(EM_interval_mean),
      sem      = sd / sqrt(n),
      ci_lower = mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sem,
      ci_upper = mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sem,
      median   = median(EM_interval_mean),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ),
  all_indiv %>%
    filter(!is.na(interval_deviation)) %>%
    group_by(species, photoperiod) %>%
    summarise(
      variable = "interval_deviation (hours from expected dark length)",
      n        = n(),
      mean     = mean(interval_deviation),
      sd       = sd(interval_deviation),
      sem      = sd / sqrt(n),
      ci_lower = mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sem,
      ci_upper = mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sem,
      median   = median(interval_deviation),
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean, sd, sem, ci_lower, ci_upper, median), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  relocate(variable, .before = species)

shapiro_results_export <- purrr::imap_dfr(all_results, function(res, nm) {
  rows <- tibble(
    variable  = nm,
    scale_tested = "raw",
    can_log   = res$can_log,
    shapiro_W = res$shapiro_raw_W,
    shapiro_p = res$shapiro_raw_p,
    normal    = res$shapiro_raw_p >= 0.05
  )

  if (isTRUE(res$shapiro_log$attempted)) {
    rows <- bind_rows(rows, tibble(
      variable = nm, scale_tested = "log", can_log = res$can_log,
      shapiro_W = res$shapiro_log$W, shapiro_p = res$shapiro_log$p,
      normal = res$shapiro_log$p >= 0.05
    ))
  }

  rows %>% mutate(final_path = res$path, final_scale_used = res$scale_used)
})

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Shapiro-Wilk results (raw and log attempts where applicable), all variables\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(shapiro_results_export)

write.csv(shapiro_results_export, "shapiro_wilk_results_all_variables.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================
# EXPORT: omnibus test tables
# ============================================================
tidy_omnibus <- function(res, nm) {
  if (res$path == "parametric") {
    tab <- res$omnibus_table
    as_tibble(tab, rownames = "term") %>%
      filter(term != "Residuals") %>%
      transmute(
        variable = nm, test_used = paste0("Two-way ANOVA (Type II, ", res$scale_used, " scale)"), term,
        sum_sq = `Sum Sq`, df = Df, statistic_name = "F", statistic_value = `F value`,
        p_value = `Pr(>F)`
      )
  } else {
    tab <- res$omnibus_table
    as_tibble(tab) %>%
      transmute(
        variable = nm, test_used = "ART (ARTool, Type III)", term = Term,
        sum_sq = `Sum Sq`, df = Df, statistic_name = "F", statistic_value = `F value`,
        p_value = `Pr(>F)`
      )
  }
}

summarize_result <- function(res) {
  if (res$path == "parametric") {
    tibble(variable = res$label, statistical_path = paste0("ANOVA (", res$scale_used, " scale, residuals normal)"),
           shapiro_p_residuals = if (res$scale_used == "log") res$shapiro_log$p else res$shapiro_raw_p,
           species_p = res$omnibus_table["species", "Pr(>F)"],
           photoperiod_p = res$omnibus_table["photoperiod", "Pr(>F)"],
           interaction_p = res$omnibus_table["species:photoperiod", "Pr(>F)"],
           LD_pairwise_p = res$bracket_df$p_value[res$bracket_df$photoperiod == "LD"],
           SD_pairwise_p = res$bracket_df$p_value[res$bracket_df$photoperiod == "SD"])
  } else {
    tab <- res$omnibus_table
    tibble(variable = res$label, statistical_path = "ART (ARTool, Type III, residuals non-normal)",
           shapiro_p_residuals = res$shapiro_raw_p,
           species_p = tab$`Pr(>F)`[tab$Term == "species"],
           photoperiod_p = tab$`Pr(>F)`[tab$Term == "photoperiod"],
           interaction_p = tab$`Pr(>F)`[tab$Term == "species:photoperiod"],
           LD_pairwise_p = res$bracket_df$p_value[res$bracket_df$photoperiod == "LD"],
           SD_pairwise_p = res$bracket_df$p_value[res$bracket_df$photoperiod == "SD"])
  }
}

phase_interval_stats_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarize_result(res_int), summarize_result(res_dev), summarize_result(res_e)
)

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION RATE: OVERALL TEST (Fisher's exact test)
# Detected vs. not-detected counts are compared across the four
# species x photoperiod groups, separately for M- and E-peaks.
# Fisher's exact test is used because detection is at or near 100%
# in several groups; it is exact and valid with zero counts, whereas
# a logistic regression model cannot be estimated reliably when
# groups have complete separation. The test indicates whether the
# four groups differ, not which factor is responsible; the pairwise
# tests below identify which groups differ.
# ============================================================
detection_contingency <- function(df, has_peak_col) {
  table(
    group    = paste(df$species, df$photoperiod, sep = "_"),
    detected = factor(df[[has_peak_col]], levels = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                      labels = c("detected", "not_detected"))
  )
}

safe_fisher <- function(tab) {
  tryCatch(fisher.test(tab), error = function(e) {
    warning("Fisher's test could not be computed (", conditionMessage(e),
            ") -- most likely every individual in every group was detected.")
    NULL
  })
}

tab_M <- detection_contingency(all_indiv, "has_M_peak")
tab_E <- detection_contingency(all_indiv, "has_E_peak")
fisher_M <- safe_fisher(tab_M)
fisher_E <- safe_fisher(tab_E)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Fisher's exact test: does the peak DETECTION rate differ across the\n")
cat("four species x photoperiod groups? -- M-peak\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(tab_M)
print(fisher_M)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Fisher's exact test: does the peak DETECTION rate differ across the\n")
cat("four species x photoperiod groups? -- E-peak\n")
cat("(with detection failures in only 1 of 4 groups, this test has very\n")
cat("little power -- interpret a non-significant result as 'not enough\n")
cat("data to detect a difference', not as evidence of no difference)\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(tab_E)
print(fisher_E)

peak_detection_fisher_summary <- tibble(
  peak_type = c("M", "E"),
  p_value   = c(if (is.null(fisher_M)) NA_real_ else fisher_M$p.value,
                if (is.null(fisher_E)) NA_real_ else fisher_E$p.value)
)
write.csv(peak_detection_fisher_summary, "peak_detection_fisher_test.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION RATE: PAIRWISE FISHER'S TESTS
# All six pairwise comparisons among the four groups, Holm-adjusted
# across all six; the two within-photoperiod species comparisons are
# then extracted (as for the continuous variables).
# Odds ratio = odds of detection in group1 / odds in group2.
# ============================================================
pairwise_fisher_detection <- function(df, has_peak_col, label) {
  d <- df %>%
    mutate(group = paste(species, photoperiod, sep = "_")) %>%
    select(group, has_peak = all_of(has_peak_col))

  groups <- sort(unique(d$group))
  pairs  <- combn(groups, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pr) {
    sub <- d %>% filter(group %in% pr)
    # Keep both detected/not-detected columns even when one is empty.
    tab <- table(factor(sub$group, levels = pr),
                 factor(sub$has_peak, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
    ft  <- fisher.test(tab)
    tibble(
      comparison = label,
      group1 = pr[1], group2 = pr[2],
      pct_detected_group1 = round(100 * mean(sub$has_peak[sub$group == pr[1]]), 1),
      pct_detected_group2 = round(100 * mean(sub$has_peak[sub$group == pr[2]]), 1),
      odds_ratio_detection = unname(ft$estimate),
      ci_lower = ft$conf.int[1], ci_upper = ft$conf.int[2],
      p_value = ft$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
    mutate(p_holm6 = p.adjust(p_value, method = "holm"),
           significance = sig_stars(p_holm6))
}

fisher_pairwise_M <- pairwise_fisher_detection(all_indiv, "has_M_peak", "M_detection")
fisher_pairwise_E <- pairwise_fisher_detection(all_indiv, "has_E_peak", "E_detection")

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Full 6-way pairwise Fisher's tests on detection rate (Holm-corrected across all 6) -- M-peak\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(fisher_pairwise_M)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Full 6-way pairwise Fisher's tests on detection rate (Holm-corrected across all 6) -- E-peak\n")
cat("(most cells are at 100% detection, so interpret with the same\n")
cat("low-power caveat as the omnibus E-peak test above)\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(fisher_pairwise_E)

peak_detection_pairwise_full6 <- bind_rows(fisher_pairwise_M, fisher_pairwise_E)

peak_detection_within_photoperiod <- bind_rows(
  extract_within_photoperiod(fisher_pairwise_M, "M_detection"),
  extract_within_photoperiod(fisher_pairwise_E, "E_detection")
)

cat("Within-photoperiod comparisons (Cxpip vs Cxquin) extracted from the\n")
cat("globally-corrected 6-way family -- species effect on peak detection\n")

# ============================================================
# PEAK DETECTION RATE PLOT
# M- and E-peak detection rates (after manual verification; manually
# excluded peaks count as not detected) per species, one panel per
# photoperiod, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals. Brackets show
# the within-photoperiod species comparisons (pairwise Fisher's
# tests, Holm-adjusted).
# ============================================================
# ---- 95% Wilson score confidence interval for a proportion. Unlike
#      a standard-error interval, it stays within 0-1 and has non-zero
#      width when all individuals in a group were detected. ----
wilson_ci <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z      <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  p      <- x / n
  denom  <- 1 + z^2 / n
  center <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / denom
  half   <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / denom
  c(lower = max(0, center - half), upper = min(1, center + half))
}

peak_detect_long <- peak_detection_summary %>%
  select(species, photoperiod, n_total, n_M_detected, n_E_detected) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(n_M_detected, n_E_detected),
               names_to = "peak_type", values_to = "n_detected") %>%
  mutate(
    peak_type    = if_else(peak_type == "n_M_detected", "M", "E"),
    pct_detected = 100 * n_detected / n_total,
    ci           = purrr::map2(n_detected, n_total, wilson_ci),
    ci_lower     = 100 * purrr::map_dbl(ci, "lower"),
    ci_upper     = 100 * purrr::map_dbl(ci, "upper"),
    photoperiod  = factor(photoperiod, levels = c("LD", "SD"))
  ) %>%
  select(-ci)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("Peak detection rate with 95% Wilson score confidence intervals\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(peak_detect_long %>% mutate(across(c(pct_detected, ci_lower, ci_upper), ~ round(.x, 1))))

write.csv(peak_detect_long %>% mutate(across(c(pct_detected, ci_lower, ci_upper), ~ round(.x, 2))),
          "peak_detection_rate_wilson_CI.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Horizontal offset of the E and M bars from each species' center
# (position_dodge(width = 0.7) with two bars).
dodge_offset <- 0.7 / 4

# Bracket spacing, based on the highest bar across both panels so
# spacing is the same in each panel.
global_max <- max(peak_detect_long$pct_detected, na.rm = TRUE)
gap_unit   <- global_max * 0.10
tick_len   <- global_max * 0.025
label_pad  <- global_max * 0.04

bracket_detect <- peak_detection_within_photoperiod %>%
  mutate(
    peak_type   = str_remove(comparison, "_detection"),
    photoperiod = factor(photoperiod, levels = c("LD", "SD")),
    x_g1  = if_else(str_detect(group1, "Cxpip"), 1, 2),
    x_g2  = if_else(str_detect(group2, "Cxpip"), 1, 2),
    dodge = if_else(peak_type == "E", -dodge_offset, dodge_offset),
    x1    = x_g1 + dodge,
    x2    = x_g2 + dodge
  )

# Height of the taller of the two bars each bracket connects, using
# the upper confidence limit so brackets clear the error bars.
bar_heights <- peak_detect_long %>%
  select(species, photoperiod, peak_type, pct_detected = ci_upper)

bracket_detect <- bracket_detect %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    bar_max_local = max(
      bar_heights$pct_detected[bar_heights$photoperiod == photoperiod &
                                 bar_heights$peak_type == peak_type],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Stack the brackets in each panel: E bracket below, M bracket above,
# each gap_unit above the taller of its own bars or the previous
# bracket.
stack_brackets <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>% arrange(factor(peak_type, levels = c("E", "M")))
  running_max <- 0
  y_pos <- numeric(nrow(df))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
    running_max <- max(running_max, df$bar_max_local[i]) + gap_unit
    y_pos[i] <- running_max
  }
  df$y_pos <- y_pos
  df
}

bracket_detect <- bracket_detect %>%
  group_by(photoperiod) %>%
  group_modify(~ stack_brackets(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(tick = tick_len)

bracket_detect_segments <- bind_rows(
  bracket_detect %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = x1, xend = x2, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos),
  bracket_detect %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = x1, xend = x1, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos - tick),
  bracket_detect %>% transmute(photoperiod, x = x2, xend = x2, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos - tick)
)

y_axis_top <- max(c(peak_detect_long$pct_detected, bracket_detect$y_pos), na.rm = TRUE) + gap_unit * 1.5

# Bracket labels ("ns" and asterisks), bold at SIG_LABEL_SIZE, drawn
# with vjust = 0 just above the bracket line.
bracket_detect_ns    <- bracket_detect %>% filter(!str_detect(significance, "\\*"))
bracket_detect_stars <- bracket_detect %>% filter(str_detect(significance, "\\*"))

p_detect <- ggplot(peak_detect_long, aes(x = species, y = pct_detected, fill = peak_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6, color = "black") +
  # 95% Wilson CI error bars (grey on the black M bars for contrast).
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper, colour = peak_type),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(M = "grey60", E = "black"), guide = "none") +
  geom_segment(data = bracket_detect_segments,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = bracket_detect_ns,
            aes(x = (x1 + x2) / 2, y = y_pos + label_pad * 0.15, label = significance),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = SIG_LABEL_SIZE, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0) +
  geom_text(data = bracket_detect_stars,
            aes(x = (x1 + x2) / 2, y = y_pos + label_pad * 0.15, label = significance),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = SIG_LABEL_SIZE, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0) +
  facet_grid(. ~ photoperiod, switch = "x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_axis_top), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Cxpip", "Cxquin"), labels = species_labels) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(M = "black", E = "white"),
                    labels = c(M = "Mpeak", E = "Epeak"),
                    name = NULL) +
  # End the y-axis line at 100%; the space above holds the brackets
  # (guide_axis(cap = ...) requires ggplot2 >= 3.5.0).
  guides(y = guide_axis(cap = "upper")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Peak detection rate (%)",
       title = "Peak detection rate, by group and peak type",
       subtitle = "After manual verification layer; error bars = 95% Wilson CI\nBrackets: within-photoperiod species comparisons (Fisher's exact, Holm-corrected)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey85", color = "grey40"),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        # Center the y-axis title on the 0-100% axis line.
        axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 50 / y_axis_top))

p_detect
ggsave("Fig_peak_detection_rate_SDvsLD.png", p_detect,
       device = ragg::agg_png, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 800)
```
